title: Voltage gains did not ensure long-window signal-to-noise gains in two partial adult worm circuit models
abstract: We tested whether remote voltage gains after electrical link loss imply better signal-to-noise ratio in two partial adult C. elegans maps. A passive model used uniform leak and equal independent white current noise. At leak equal to 0.1 times median weighted degree, 476 of 15,702 voltage gains above 10% in adult 7 and 156 of 5,460 in adult 8 gave no long-window signal-to-noise gain. With intact attenuation at least 0.1, these counts were 159 of 1,897 and 57 of 1,141. Most voltage gains still gave signal-to-noise gains. Two selected examples had voltage ratios 1.154 and 1.110 but long-window signal-to-noise ratios 0.731 and 0.734. Unit link weights preserved the mismatch; large leak removed it from the tested substantial-baseline cases. All 496 primary link updates passed direct solves. Noise observation time changes the result. Partial maps, assumed passive parameters, and no matched activity data prevent claims about live-animal reliability. Code, hashes, selected graphs, per-link counts, finite-window checks, and a figure support reproduction.

display.caption: Voltage gains and signal-to-noise gains after link loss. The noise observation window and leak change the result in two partial adult worm models.
